title: Engagement profile
description: The engagement record configuration writes at setup, and the thing three skills declared as a required input while nothing produced it (finding F1). It is configuration, not intake: invariant 23 had already decided that config writes the engagement record, so the gap was a missing contract rather than a missing design. Its fields carry a stated basis rather than a figure envelope, because a configured baseline is not read from a client document and must not pretend to be.

practice.description: Practice group. Validated against the Scope Registry at resolve time (P05); this schema only enforces the shape, because the taxonomy is versioned separately from the contract.

disposition.description: Repeat or new client. This is what routes prior-year roll-forward against first-year baseline, and what scopes precedent retrieval to the client's own decisions.

industry_classification.description: GPC Scrub screens against this and Cost of Capital picks its industry premium from it. A contested classification is an escalation in both skills, which is only possible because it is recorded here rather than guessed per skill.

scale_convention.description: The scale this engagement's working papers are kept in. It is a presentation convention only - it never becomes the default for a figure whose own scale was not read.

owner_compensation_baseline.description: The benchmark officer-compensation tests are run against. Required: EBITDA Normalization escalates rather than proceeding when there is no benchmark, and a profile that omits this silently is exactly how that escalation gets skipped.

materiality_threshold.description: Optional here; the Constraint Registry carries the firm floor and a profile may only sit at or below it.

checkpoint_policy.description: How much a human reviews on this engagement. Read by exactly one node, the Confidence Router. It can raise the bar - a higher confidence floor, more always-review categories, a tighter review level per skill - and never lower one: the Checkpoint Policy refuses a review floor below what the skill declares, and a materiality threshold above the firm floor is refused where materiality_threshold is read. There is no auto-accept default; a policy that sets none auto-accepts nothing.

owner.description: The named person the review queue escalates to. Required: an item with no owner is an item nobody works.

auto_accept_confidence.description: Items at or above this confidence, material to nobody and flagged by nothing, go straight through. Absent means nothing is auto-accepted.

review_floors.description: skill name -> a value on the review ladder in scopes.yaml, at or above what the skill declares.
review_floors.x-open-by-design: A map keyed by skill name; the skill names are the Skill Registry's, versioned separately from this contract, and each value is checked against the review ladder at policy load. Closing the key set here would pin the skill tree into the profile contract.

statements_arrive_in.description: The scale the client's own statements are stated in: 1 for units, 1000 for thousands, 1000000 for millions. Optional, and there is no default. A client may send financials in any form and the firm always restates them to thousands, so what arrived has to be established rather than assumed - thousands read as units is a figure out by a factor of a thousand, and it passes every other check on the way through. The readers settle this from a cue on the page where there is one; this is where a person settles it where there is not, and a cue on the page always wins.
